That voicing still works under the motif, but a true C/E would be **E₃ – G₃ – C₄**. Either one sounds fine there.

Get some rest. The motif will still be there tomorrow, and fresh ears are great for hearing which version feels right.

# Left-Hand Voicings (Middle-C Area)

**Notation:** Middle C = **C4**. C3 is the C one octave below. Fingerings are listed bottom to top (5 = pinky, 1 = thumb).

**General fingering rule for 3-note LH triads:**
- Root position: **5-3-1**
- First inversion: **5-3-1** (5-2-1 also works if it feels better)
- Second inversion: **5-2-1**

## 1. A Natural Minor
| Chord | Position | Notes | Fingering |
|---|---|---|---|
| Am (i) | Root | A2 – C3 – E3 | 5-3-1 |
| Am/C | 1st inv | C3 – E3 – A3 | 5-3-1 |
| C (III) | Root | C3 – E3 – G3 | 5-3-1 |
| C/E | 1st inv | E3 – G3 – C4 | 5-3-1 |

## 2. A Harmonic Minor
| Chord | Position | Notes | Fingering |
|---|---|---|---|
| Am (i) | Root | A2 – C3 – E3 | 5-3-1 |
| Am/C | 1st inv | C3 – E3 – A3 | 5-3-1 |
| E (V) | Root | E3 – **G#3** – B3 | 5-3-1 |
| E/G# | 1st inv | **G#2** – B2 – E3 | 5-3-1 |

**Tip:** E/G# → Am root position is very smooth. G# moves up to A, B moves up to C, and E stays put.

## 3. A Melodic Minor
| Chord | Position | Notes | Fingering |
|---|---|---|---|
| Am (i) | Root | A2 – C3 – E3 | 5-3-1 |
| D (IV, raised 6th) | Root | D3 – **F#3** – A3 | 5-3-1 |
| D/F# | 1st inv | **F#3** – A3 – D4 | 5-3-1 |
| E (V) | Root | E3 – **G#3** – B3 | 5-3-1 |
| E/G# | 1st inv | **G#2** – B2 – E3 | 5-3-1 |

**Descending:** use Am, or C (natural-minor chords). Avoid F# and G# on the way down.

## 4. C Natural Minor
| Chord | Position | Notes | Fingering |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cm (i) | Root | C3 – Eb3 – G3 | 5-3-1 |
| Cm/Eb | 1st inv | Eb3 – G3 – C4 | 5-3-1 |
| Ab (VI) | Root | Ab2 – C3 – Eb3 | 5-3-1 |
| Ab/C | 1st inv | C3 – Eb3 – Ab3 | 5-3-1 |

## 5a. C Harmonic Minor
| Chord | Position | Notes | Fingering |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cm (i) | Root | C3 – Eb3 – G3 | 5-3-1 |
| Cm/Eb | 1st inv | Eb3 – G3 – C4 | 5-3-1 |
| G (V) | Root | G2 – **B2** – D3 | 5-3-1 |
| G/B | 1st inv | **B2** – D3 – G3 | 5-3-1 |

**Tip:** G/B → Cm root position. B moves up to C, D moves up to Eb, and G stays.

## 5b. C Melodic Minor
| Chord | Position | Notes | Fingering |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cm (i) | Root | C3 – Eb3 – G3 | 5-3-1 |
| F (IV, raised 6th) | Root | F3 – **A3** – C4 | 5-3-1 |
| F/A | 1st inv | **A2** – C3 – F3 | 5-3-1 |
| G (V) | Root | G2 – **B2** – D3 | 5-3-1 |
| G/B | 1st inv | **B2** – D3 – G3 | 5-3-1 |

**Descending:** return to Cm and Ab (natural-minor chords) with Bb and Ab in the melody.

---

# 4-Bar Cadences: i – iv – V7 – i

These are in 4/4 time. The right hand plays eighth notes, and the left hand holds one chord per bar (whole notes). The LH voicings are chosen so each finger moves a step or less between chords.

**V7 tip:** A full four-note V7 is a stretch for many hands, so this version uses three notes (root, 3rd, 7th, with the 5th omitted). It still sounds like a complete V7.

## A Minor: Am – Dm – E7 – Am

| Bar | Chord | LH (fingering) | RH (8 eighth notes) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Am | A2 – C3 – E3 (5-3-1) | C4 E4 G4 A4 G4 E4 C4 E4 |
| 2 | Dm/A | A2 – D3 – F3 (5-2-1) | D4 F4 A4 G4 F4 E4 D4 F4 |
| 3 | E7 | **G#2** – D3 – E3 (5-2-1) | E4 **G#4** B4 **G#4** E4 D4 E4 **G#4** |
| 4 | Am | A2 – C3 – E3 (5-3-1) | A4 E4 C4 E4 A4 (half note) |

**Listen for:** G# → A in both hands at the bar 3 → bar 4 change (RH G#4 → A4, LH G#2 → A2). That is the harmonic-minor leading tone resolving.

## C Minor: Cm – Fm – G7 – Cm

| Bar | Chord | LH (fingering) | RH (8 eighth notes) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cm | C3 – Eb3 – G3 (5-3-1) | C4 Eb4 G4 Ab4 G4 Eb4 C4 Eb4 |
| 2 | Fm/C | C3 – F3 – Ab3 (5-2-1) | F4 Ab4 C5 Bb4 Ab4 G4 F4 Ab4 |
| 3 | G7 | **B2** – F3 – G3 (5-2-1) | G4 **B4** D5 **B4** G4 F4 G4 **B4** |
| 4 | Cm | C3 – Eb3 – G3 (5-3-1) | C5 G4 Eb4 G4 C5 (half note) |

**Listen for:** B → C at the bar 3 → bar 4 change (RH B4 → C5, LH B2 → C3).

**Notes:**
- Bar 1 of each cadence is your original motif.
- In both bar 2s, the iv chord is in second inversion (fingered 5-2-1). This keeps the left hand nearly still.
- The Bb in bar 2 of the C minor version is fine because the melody is descending. Only the V7 bar needs the raised 7th (B natural).

## Practice Steps
1. Play the LH chords alone, holding each for four slow beats. Feel how little your hand moves.
2. Play the RH alone, slowly and evenly.
3. Put the hands together at a slow tempo (around ♩ = 60).
4. Once that feels comfortable, try playing the LH as two half notes per bar (repeating the chord on beat 3) for a bit more motion.

# 4-Bar Cadences: i – iv⁶ – V(7) – i

**Fingering key:** 1 = thumb, 5 = pinky. LH is listed bottom to top. RH fingerings line up under each note.

## A Minor: Am – Dm/F – E (or E7) – Am

| Bar | Chord | LH (fingering) | RH notes | RH fingering |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Am | A2 – C3 – E3 (5-3-1) | C4 E4 G4 A4 G4 E4 C4 E4 | 1 2 4 5 4 2 1 2 |
| 2 | Dm/F | F2 – A2 – D3 (5-3-1) | D4 F4 A4 G4 F4 E4 D4 F4 | 1 3 5 4 3 2 1 3 |
| 3a | **E** (triad) | G#2 – B2 – E3 (5-3-1) | E4 G#4 B4 G#4 E4 G#4 B4 G#4 | 1 3 5 3 1 3 5 3 |
| 3b | **E7** | G#2 – D3 – E3 (5-2-1) | E4 G#4 B4 G#4 E4 D4 E4 G#4 | 2 3 5 3 2 1 2 3 |
| 4 | Am | A2 – C3 – E3 (5-3-1) | A4 E4 C4 E4 A4 (half note) | 5 2 1 2 5 |

**LH voice leading:**
- **Dm/F → E:** every note moves up a step (F→G#, A→B, D→E).
- **E → Am:** G#→A, B→C, and E stays.
- **E7 → Am:** G#→A, D→C, and E stays.

## C Minor: Cm – Fm/Ab – G (or G7) – Cm

| Bar | Chord | LH (fingering) | RH notes | RH fingering |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cm | C3 – Eb3 – G3 (5-3-1) | C4 Eb4 G4 Ab4 G4 Eb4 C4 Eb4 | 1 2 4 5 4 2 1 2 |
| 2 | Fm/Ab | Ab2 – C3 – F3 (5-3-1) | F4 Ab4 C5 Bb4 Ab4 G4 F4 Ab4 | 1 3 5 4 3 2 1 3 |
| 3a | **G** (triad) | B2 – D3 – G3 (5-3-1) | G4 B4 D5 B4 G4 B4 D5 B4 | 1 3 5 3 1 3 5 3 |
| 3b | **G7** | B2 – F3 – G3 (5-2-1) | G4 B4 D5 B4 G4 F4 G4 B4 | 2 3 5 3 2 1 2 3 |
| 4 | Cm | C3 – Eb3 – G3 (5-3-1) | C5 G4 Eb4 G4 C5 (half note) | 5 2 1 2 5 |

**LH voice leading:**
- **Fm/Ab → G:** every note moves up a step (Ab→B, C→D, F→G).
- **G → Cm:** B→C, D→Eb, and G stays.
- **G7 → Cm:** B→C, F→Eb, and G stays.

## Notes
- **Triad vs. V7 melody:** the triad version (3a) leaves the 7th (D or F) out of the RH, so the chord stays a plain triad. The V7 version (3b) includes it.
- **Position shifts:**
  - **Into bar 2:** the thumb tucks under to start the new five-finger position.
  - **Into bar 3a:** the thumb crosses under from finger 3.
  - **Into bar 4:** finger 3 on the leading tone moves up to 5 on the tonic.
- **The 3b stretch:** fingers 2–5 span a 5th. If that feels wide, start with the triad version (3a).
- **Practice:** hands separately first, then together at about ♩ = 60.

**Format:** `Bar | Chord | LH (whole note) | RH pitches(finger)`
Bar 4 RH = four eighths + one half note (marked `-half`).

### 1. A Minor, Triad V (Am – Dm/F – E – Am)

# ABC Notation (4 Cadences)

ABC is the most compact option. Each cadence is a separate tune (X:1–4), so you can paste them all at once or one at a time.

**Format notes:**
- **Fingerings:** written as `!1!`–`!5!` before each RH note. These are standard ABC fingering marks.
- **LH chords:** whole notes, with fingerings in `%` comments.
- **Octaves:** `C` = C4 (middle C), `c` = C5, `C,` = C3, `C,,` = C2.
- **Accidentals:** G# and B natural are written out every time for clarity.

```abc
X:1
T:A minor - Triad V (Am - Dm/F - E - Am)
M:4/4
L:1/8
Q:1/4=60
K:Am
V:RH clef=treble
V:LH clef=bass
% LH fingering: all 5-3-1
[V:RH] !1!C !2!E !4!G !5!A !4!G !2!E !1!C !2!E | !1!D !3!F !5!A !4!G !3!F !2!E !1!D !3!F | !1!E !3!^G !5!B !3!^G !1!E !3!^G !5!B !3!^G | !5!A !2!E !1!C !2!E !5!A4 |]
[V:LH] [A,,C,E,]8 | [F,,A,,D,]8 | [^G,,B,,E,]8 | [A,,C,E,]8 |]

X:2
T:A minor - V7 (Am - Dm/F - E7 - Am)
M:4/4
L:1/8
Q:1/4=60
K:Am
V:RH clef=treble
V:LH clef=bass
% LH fingering: 5-3-1, 5-3-1, 5-2-1 (E7), 5-3-1
[V:RH] !1!C !2!E !4!G !5!A !4!G !2!E !1!C !2!E | !1!D !3!F !5!A !4!G !3!F !2!E !1!D !3!F | !2!E !3!^G !5!B !3!^G !2!E !1!D !2!E !3!^G | !5!A !2!E !1!C !2!E !5!A4 |]
[V:LH] [A,,C,E,]8 | [F,,A,,D,]8 | [^G,,D,E,]8 | [A,,C,E,]8 |]

X:3
T:C minor - Triad V (Cm - Fm/Ab - G - Cm)
M:4/4
L:1/8
Q:1/4=60
K:Cm
V:RH clef=treble
V:LH clef=bass
% LH fingering: all 5-3-1
[V:RH] !1!C !2!E !4!G !5!A !4!G !2!E !1!C !2!E | !1!F !3!A !5!c !4!B !3!A !2!G !1!F !3!A | !1!G !3!=B !5!d !3!=B !1!G !3!=B !5!d !3!=B | !5!c !2!G !1!E !2!G !5!c4 |]
[V:LH] [C,E,G,]8 | [A,,C,F,]8 | [=B,,D,G,]8 | [C,E,G,]8 |]

X:4
T:C minor - V7 (Cm - Fm/Ab - G7 - Cm)
M:4/4
L:1/8
Q:1/4=60
K:Cm
V:RH clef=treble
V:LH clef=bass
% LH fingering: 5-3-1, 5-3-1, 5-2-1 (G7), 5-3-1
[V:RH] !1!C !2!E !4!G !5!A !4!G !2!E !1!C !2!E | !1!F !3!A !5!c !4!B !3!A !2!G !1!F !3!A | !2!G !3!=B !5!d !3!=B !2!G !1!F !2!G !3!=B | !5!c !2!G !1!E !2!G !5!c4 |]
[V:LH] [C,E,G,]8 | [A,,C,F,]8 | [=B,,F,G,]8 | [C,E,G,]8 |]
```

**C minor note:** `K:Cm` puts Bb, Eb, and Ab in the key signature. That means plain `E`, `A`, and `B` play as Eb, Ab, and Bb, and `=B` is B natural.

## Getting It Into Your DAW
Most DAWs import **MIDI** or **MusicXML** rather than ABC, so convert it first:
- **EasyABC** (free): paste the code, then use File → Export → MusicXML or MIDI. MusicXML keeps the fingerings.
- **abcjs.net editor** (browser): paste the code to preview and download MIDI.
- **MuseScore:** import the MusicXML from EasyABC, then export to any format.

If you'd prefer LilyPond, I can provide that version too.
